artifacts.summary: 5-phase plan (6h, 4 waves) retracting sapience write-tool grants via forced-reload retraction in the merge engine, regression coverage, two caveat rewrites, and a five-repository redeploy.

memory_candidates.content: Retraction in the Neovim extension merge engine is a call-site gap, not a missing mechanism. Three separate facts compose into the bug: (1) deep_merge is additive-only by design and records every fragment item on every merge so unload always has something to remove; (2) M.unmerge_settings plus build_retained_fragments IS a working, sibling-safe retraction primitive, but is reached only from manager.unload; (3) manager.resync_all -- the path deploy-headless.sh's default mode uses -- deliberately 'never unloads', force-reloading each extension in place. So a narrowed fragment never propagates to an already-loaded repository. The load-time hook orphan sweep is the one load-path retraction that works, and it is explicitly scoped to the hooks key only (permissions/env/mcpServers are read and rewritten byte-for-byte). deploy-headless.sh --wipe is not a workaround: settings_backup snapshots and restores settings.local.json byte-for-byte rather than re-merging from fragments. The fix shape is to call the existing unmerge with the extension's own prior merged_sections immediately before process_merge_targets in manager.load's opts.force branch. The discrimination rule that protects a hand-added user grant needs no invention: remove_tracked visits only keys present in the passed tracked structure, so an untracked grant is never a candidate.
